editorial score 3 is below 4

editorial: The title promises every signal, but logs were off and no HTTP metrics were counted. What the post shows is traces, the service map, JVM metrics and connection-pool metrics. Fix: Retitle around what was measured and credit the product, e.g. 'One Env Var, a Full Splunk APM Service Map: What the OTel Java Agent Gave a Spring Boot App, and What It Cost'

technical: The 'with agent' run also added the Collector DaemonSet on the same node, so two things changed between runs. Startup, memory pressure and p95 can't be credited to the agent alone. Fix: Install the Collector before reproduce.sh measures the baseline, so the only difference between runs is JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS. Then rerun and update the cost table.

technical: The brief promised HTTP metrics and they're missing. The agent_names query only looks at deployment.environment and k8s.cluster.name-scoped series, and it stopped at 206 s. Fix: Query sf_metric:http.server.request.duration* and http.client.request.duration* by sf_service or service.name, wait at least one more export interval, and report the result. Otherwise drop HTTP from the takeaway.

technical: Step 1 of the post can't be reproduced, because the Terraform has no variable or provider declarations. Fix: Commit variables.tf (region, lab_name, permissions_boundary defaulting to null) and provider "aws" { region = var.region }, so `terraform init && terraform apply` works as the post says.

editorial: The TL;DR gives the overhead numbers as facts, with no caveat that they come from one run on a contended burstable node at 100m CPU request. Fix: Add 'in one run, two JVMs starting together on one t3.large with 100m CPU requests' to the TL;DR. Also report the spread of the three startup samples, not only the median.
outside claim without a known source: The JVM reads JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS at startup by itself, so one variable can attach and configure the agent
The core numbers trace back to fix.sh output: 3 map nodes including the inferred Postgres, 4 spans pulled from Splunk APM by a known trace ID, 19 metric names, and the jar SHA-256 unchanged.

The cost comparison changes two things at once. fix.sh installs the Splunk OTel Collector DaemonSet on the same t3.large before it measures the 'with agent' run, while reproduce.sh measured the baseline with no Collector. So the 18 s startup and the p95 figures can't be credited to the agent alone.

The repo can't be reproduced as published. main.tf uses var.lab_name and var.permissions_boundary and has no provider block, the README tells readers to declare these themselves, and the post's Step 1 says plain `terraform apply` works.

Each overhead figure comes from one run: the median of 3 startups, a single RSS sample and about 1,200 requests at roughly 20 rps on burstable nodes. The post admits this, which is good, but the TL;DR states the figures with no caveat.

Clear reader and decision. The 18 s startup hit and the roughly 92 MiB of memory outside -Xmx are real findings the docs don't give, and the probe and memory-limit advice is something a reader can act on.
The title says 'Every Signal', but the post itself rules out logs and couldn't find HTTP metrics, so the title promises more than the body shows.
The TL;DR and the 'The trick' / 'The proof' headings read as stock template. The 'Time and cost' bullet mixes wall-clock time with overhead.
The 'What I didn't test' section is honest and useful.
There is no search or traffic data, and the brief rates demand 'weak'.

The one demand signal, issue 21136, is about Logback baggage MDC entries missing from exported log attributes. It isn't a user checking which attributes the agent exports, and it concerns logs, which this post turns off. It doesn't back this topic.
The headline wording ('Every Signal') isn't backed by evidence that readers search in those terms.

claims.text: The JVM reads JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS at startup by itself, so one variable can attach and configure the agent
The OpenTelemetry performance guide covers how to reduce agent overhead
The added 92 to 94 MiB sits outside the -Xmx setting
Hand-written spans can follow for business steps the agent can't know about

brief.reader: Platform engineer rolling out observability to Java teams on Kubernetes
brief.decision: Whether to turn on the OTel Java agent everywhere first, before asking any team for code changes
brief.question: What exactly do I get in Splunk Observability Cloud from the OTel Java agent alone, and what does it cost my service?
brief.takeaway: You can show a team its service map, traces and JVM and HTTP metrics from one environment variable, and quote measured startup, memory and p95 numbers when they ask what it costs.
brief.adds: Existing pages list what the agent can emit and how to tune overhead. This post shows what one small Spring Boot system really produced in Splunk, and measures the cost on the same jar and image.
brief.open_question: With one environment variable and no code change, how many services, metric names and spans per request does the OTel Java agent put in Splunk Observability Cloud, and how much startup time, memory and p95 latency does it add to a Spring Boot service?
tradeoffs: Agent on every service first, or hand-written instrumentation later
Default settings, or tuning instrumentation and sampling for lower overhead
Traces and metrics reach Observability Cloud here; application logs follow a separate route
